chunks: Ahmad ibn al-Hasan al-Qattan and Ali ibn Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn 'Imran al-Daqqaq (may Allah have mercy on them) said: Ahmad ibn Yahya ibn Zakariyya al-Qattan said: Muhammad ibn al-Abbas said: Muhammad ibn Abi al-Sari narrated to me, saying: Ahmad ibn 'Abd Allah ibn Yunus narrated, from Sa'd al-Kufi, from al-Asbagh ibn Nubatah, who said:

When Ali ibn Abi Talib (peace be upon him) assumed the Caliphate and the people paid allegiance to him, he went out to the Mosque wearing the turban of the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family), dressed in the outer garment of the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family), wearing the shoes of the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family), and carrying the sword of the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family). He ascended the pulpit and sat firmly upon it. Then he interlaced his fingers and placed his hands below his stomach.

Then he said: O assembly of people! Ask me before you are deprived of me. This is the vessel of knowledge. This is the saliva (effect) of the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family). This is what the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) fed me like the feeding of a bird. Ask me, for indeed I have the knowledge of the First Ones and the Last Ones.

By Allah, if a cushion were folded up for me so I could sit on it, I would judge the people of the Torah with their Torah until the Torah would speak and say: 'Ali has spoken the truth, he has not lied. He has judged you with what Allah revealed in it.' And I would judge the people of the Gospel with their Gospel until the Gospel would speak and say: 'Ali has spoken the truth, he has not lied. He has judged you with what Allah revealed in it.' And I would judge the people of the Qur'an with their Qur'an until the Qur'an would speak and say: 'Ali has spoken the truth, he has not lied. He has judged you with what Allah revealed in it.'

And you recite the Qur'an by night and by day. Is there among you anyone who knows what was revealed in it? And if it were not for a verse in the Book of Allah, I would have informed you of what has been and what will be and what is to come until the Day of Judgment. And that verse is this: 'Allah erases what He wills and confirms, and with Him is the Mother of the Book.'

Then he said: Ask me before you are deprived of me. By Allah who split the grain and created the soul, if you asked me about every verse, whether revealed by night or by day, its Meccan and Medinan verses, its travel and residence contexts, its abrogating and abrogated verses, its clear and allegorical verses, and its interpretation and application, I would inform you.

A man named Dhi'lab stood up to him. He was sharp of tongue, eloquent in speech, and brave of heart. He said: 'The son of Abu Talib has certainly climbed a difficult ladder. I will surely humiliate him today for you by questioning him.'

He said: 'O Commander of the Faithful, have you seen your Lord?' He said: 'Woe to you, O Dhi'lab! I do not serve a Lord whom I have not seen. I have not seen Him.' He said: 'How did you see Him? Describe Him for us?'

He said: 'Woe to you! The eyes do not see Him through the vision of sight, but the hearts see Him through the realities of faith. Woe to you, O Dhi'lab! Indeed, my Lord cannot be described by distance, nor by movement, nor by stillness, nor by standing in an upright posture, nor by His coming or going.'

He is the Subtle of the Subtle, not described by subtlety. He is the Great of the Great, not described by greatness. He is the Grand of the Grand, not described by grandeur. He is the Majestic of the Majestic, not described by bulk. He is the Affectionate of the Affectionate, not described by delicacy. He is the Granter of Security, not through service. He is the Perceiving, not through touch. He is the Speaker, not through utterance.

He is in all things without mixture. He is outside them without separation. He is above all things, yet it is not said that something is above Him. He is in front of all things, yet it is not said that He has a front. He is inside all things, not like something inside something else. And He is outside them, not like something outside something else.
Dhi'lab fell unconscious. Then he said: 'By Allah, I have never heard a response like this. By Allah, I will not ask such a question again.' Then he said: 'Ask me before you are deprived of me.'
Al-Ash'ath ibn Qays stood up to him and said: 'O Commander of the Faithful, why is the jizyah (tax) taken from the Magians when no Book was revealed to them and no Prophet was sent to them?'

He said: 'Yes, O Ash'ath! Allah certainly revealed a Book to them and sent a Messenger to them. They had a king who got drunk one night, called his daughter to his bed, and committed incest with her. When he woke up, his people heard of it and gathered at his door.'

They said: 'O King, you have defiled and destroyed our religion. Come out so we may purify you and administer the punishment upon you.' He said to them: 'Gather and listen to my speech. If there is a way out for me from what I have done, then so be it. Otherwise, do as you please.'

They gathered, and he said to them: 'Do you know that Allah has not created a creation more honorable to Him than our father Adam and our mother Eve?' They said: 'You are right, O King.' He said: 'Is it not so that he married his sons to his daughters and his daughters to his sons?' They said: 'You are right. This is the religion.'

So they contracted upon that. Allah erased the knowledge from their chests and raised the Book from them. Thus, they are the disbelievers who enter the Fire without reckoning, and the hypocrites are worse off than them.
Al-Ash'ath said: 'By Allah, I have never heard a response like this. By Allah, I will never ask such a question again.' Then he said: 'Ask me before you are deprived of me.'

A man from the far end of the Mosque stood up, leaning on his staff. He kept moving through the people until he drew near to him. He said: 'O Commander of the Faithful, guide me to an action that, if I perform it, Allah will save me from the Fire.'

He said to him: 'Listen, O man, then understand, then be certain. This world is established on three: a speaking scholar who utilizes his knowledge, a wealthy person who is not miserly with his wealth for the people of Allah's religion, and a poor person who is patient.'

When the scholar hides his knowledge, the wealthy acts miserly, and the poor do not practice patience, then comes the affliction and ruin. At that point, the recognizers of Allah know that the house has returned to its origin, i.e., disbelief after faith.
O Questioner, do not be deceived by the multitude of mosques and the gathering of people whose bodies are united but their hearts are divided.

O Questioner, the people are of three types: the ascetic, the hedonist, and the patient. As for the ascetic, he is not pleased with anything from this world that comes to him, nor does he grieve over anything from it that departs from him.

As for the patient one, he longs for it with his heart. If he attains something from it, he turns himself away from it due to what he knows of its evil outcome. As for the hedonist, he does not care whether he attains it through permissible or forbidden means.

He said to him: 'O Commander of the Faithful, what is the sign of the believer in that time?' He said: 'He looks to what Allah has imposed upon him as a right and fulfills it. He looks to what contradicts it and distances himself from it, even if it is a close relative.'

He said: 'You are right, by Allah, O Commander of the Faithful.' Then the man disappeared, and we did not see him. The people looked for him but did not find him. Ali (peace be upon him) smiled on the pulpit and said: 'What is the matter with you? That was my brother, al-Khidr (peace be upon him).'
Then he said: 'Ask me before you are deprived of me.' No one stood up to him. So he praised Allah and extolled Him, and sent blessings upon his Prophet (peace be upon him and his family).

Then he said to al-Hasan (peace be upon him): 'O Hasan, stand up and ascend the pulpit and speak with a speech so that the Quraysh do not claim ignorance of you after me, lest they say: 'Verily, al-Hasan ibn Ali knows nothing.'

Al-Hasan (peace be upon him) said: 'O father, how can I ascend and speak when you are among the people, listening and seeing?' He said to him: 'May my father and mother be your ransom! I will conceal myself from you, and I will listen and see, while you do not see me.'
Al-Hasan (peace be upon him) ascended the pulpit, praised Allah with eloquent and noble praises, and sent blessings upon the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) with a brief prayer.

Then he said: 'O people, I heard my grandfather, the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family), say: 'I am the City of Knowledge and Ali is its gate. And does one enter the city except through its gate?'
Then he descended, and Ali (peace be upon him) leapt towards him, lifted him, and embraced him to his chest.

Then he said to al-Husayn (peace be upon him): 'O my son, stand up and ascend the pulpit and speak with a speech so that the Quraysh do not claim ignorance of you after me, lest they say: 'Verily, al-Husayn ibn Ali sees nothing.' Let your speech be subsequent to your brother's speech.'
Al-Husayn (peace be upon him) ascended the pulpit, praised Allah and extolled Him, and sent blessings upon his Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) with a brief prayer.

Then he said: 'O assembly of people, I heard my grandfather, the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family), say: 'Verily, Ali is the City of Guidance. Whoever enters it is saved, and whoever lags behind it is lost.'
Ali (peace be upon him) leapt towards him, embraced him to his chest, and kissed him.

Then he said: 'O assembly of people, bear witness that these two are the young birds (sons) of the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family), and His trust which He entrusted to me, and I entrust them to you. O people, the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) will question you about them.'

key_terms.زَقًّا زَقًا: Fed like a bird feeds its young

ai.seo_question: What are the three questions asked of Imam Ali (AS) in the Mosque of Kufa and what are their answers?
ai.summary: This foundational hadith from al-Tawhid highlights Imam Ali’s (AS) comprehensive authority (wilayah) through his mastery of the Quran's exoteric and esoteric dimensions, famously asserting that the Torah and Gospel would testify to his truth. It serves as a key text for Shia theological arguments regarding the infallible interpretation of scripture and the unique status of the Ahl al-Bayt as the inheritors of the Prophet's knowledge.
